PROBLEM & MOTIVATION
Paper diplomas and scanned PDFs are easy to forge.
Verification is manual, slow and centralized (single point of
failure).
Over-disclosure: showing a diploma exposes ID, date of birth and
GPA.
Goals: tamper-evidence, privacy-preserving selective disclosure,
cost-efficient scale, trustless verification.
1- Introduction
3

Per-credential minting on-chain: ~103,156 gas each, ≈ 1.03 billion gas per 10k
cohort.
Mandatory IPFS pinning: recurring fee ($0.001–0.01/credential/month) and gateway
dependency
ES256K SD-JWT needs a custom parser (_sd_alg, envelope overhead)
4
PHASE 2 RECAP: WHAT LIMITED US AT
UNIVERSITY SCALE
Per-credential revocation mapping: 1 storage slot per revoked credential.
In Phase 1+2 (HK251 - HK252), we designed and implemented a functional
prototype leveraging SD-JWT VC (Selective Disclosure JSON Web Token Verifiable
Credential) paired with an on-chain Merkle Tree registry. However, rigorous
evaluation at university scale (≥10,000 graduates per cohort) revealed these
significant operational bottlenecks:

Objective Technical Approach
Eliminate mandatory IPFS dependencies Self-contained off-chain JSON + EIP-712 signature
Simplify cryptographic, signing/verification Standard signTypedData / verifyTypedData (ethers v6)
Reduce on-chain gas overhead by ≥10× Off-chain signing + 1 anchorBatch per cohort
Streamlined Selective Disclosure Salted keccak256 commitments inside the signed struct
 Gas-optimized Revocation Management On-chain bitmap (256 creds/word)
High-throughput Processing (≥500 cred/sec) Modular TypeScript SDK + chunked bulk engine

RELATED WORK

Foundations: VC Model and the Move from SD-JWT to EIP-712
7
 2 – THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS
Issuer–Holder–Verifier trust triangle (W3C VC).
SD-JWT: salted disclosures + _sd[] digests.
Limitation noted in Phase 2: ES256K is not natively supported by standard JWT
libraries, so a custom parser was needed.
EIP-712: typed structured data, domain separator (name, version, chainId,
verifyingContract), and wallet and ethers v6 support.

8
FOUR BUILDING BLOCKS

3 - SYSTEM DESIGN
9
Overall Architecture
Off-chain layer (zero gas): Issuer Portal → EIP-712 SDK (sign, create disclosure) → batch of N
signed credentials + StandardMerkleTree.
On-chain trust anchor (Sepolia): IssuerRegistry (who may sign) and CredentialRegistryV3
(anchorBatch, isRevoked).
Application layer: Issuer, Holder, Verifier, Admin portals on Next.js 14 + Prisma + PostgreSQL.
Only one transaction per cohort: anchorBatch(root).

CREDENTIAL SCHEMA (EIP-712)
11
BkCredential: credId, issuedAt, batchId, publicClaims (nested), privateClaims[] (bytes32
commitments), merkleRoot.
PublicClaims: vct, degreeTitle, graduationDate, honors.
Private claims (name, student ID, DOB, GPA) are stored only as salted commitments.
Holder file = credential + Merkle proof + 65-byte signature + disclosure objects.

SMART CONTRACT DESIGN
11
IssuerRegistry (Ownable2Step): addSigner, revokeSigner, isSigner, DID labels, paginated
getters.
CredentialRegistryV3 (Ownable2Step + Pausable): anchorBatch(root, size, ipfsCid), revoke,
revokeBatch, isRevoked, getAnchor.
Cross-contract check: onlySigner calls IssuerRegistry.isSigner(msg.sender).
Emergency pause; two-step ownership transfer.

ISSUANCE AND REVOCATION WORKFLOWS
12
Issuance (8 steps): CSV upload → Zod validation → UUID → salts and commitments → EIP-712
signing → Merkle tree and proofs → anchorBatch → persist (PostgreSQL).
Revocation: admin calls revoke or revokeBatch → bit set in bitmap → DB audit log
synchronized.

4 - IMPLEMENTATION
Contracts: Solidity, Hardhat, OpenZeppelin v5, solidity-coverage, hardhat-gas-reporter
App: Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Prisma v6, PostgreSQL on Neon, Privy passwordless login.
@bkcred/sdk modules: domain, signer, verifier, disclosure, merkle, index.
14
Deployed on Ethereum Sepolia; addresses recorded in deployments-v3.json
Smart ContractFullstack Application

BACKEND ARCHITECTURE & ASYNCHRONOUS JOB MANAGER
15

FOUR WEB PORTALS
Issuer: CSV ingest, live SSE stepper, anchorBatch trigger.
Holder: Privy email login, credential vault, selective disclosure toggles, JSON
presentation export.
Verifier: drag-and-drop JSON or deep link, live 10-step stepper.
Admin: signer lifecycle, bitmap revocation, emergency pause.

97 automated tests, all passing: 52 contract tests (20 + 32) and 45 SDK tests.
100% statements, branches, functions and lines on both contracts.
STRIDE threat matrix: 6 categories mapped to mitigations.
33/33 exploit simulations rejected: Merkle tampering (8), signature forgery (7),
selective-disclosure attacks (6), bitmap revocation attacks (6), replay and domain
collision (6).

EMPIRICAL EVALUATION: SCENARIOS A–E

O(1) Constant-Time Scaling: Anchoring cost remains constant regardless of cohort size
via single Merkle root submission.
1,430x Gas Reduction (N = 10,000): Slashes on-chain consumption from ~240M to
167,804 gas (~16.8 gas / credential).
Live Sepolia Testnet Validation: 10,000-cohort anchored in block 11,654,826 for only
0.00019 ETH ($0.56) with 100% pass rate.
ON-CHAIN COST AND LIVE SEPOLIA VALIDATION

Instant emergency containment;
avoids EVM timestamp attacks

and cost ~1000x more gas

6 – EVALUATION, LIMITATION, FUTURE WORK
20

Deploy on Layer 2 (Arbitrum / Base / Optimism).
ZK range proofs (e.g., GPA ≥ 3.2 without revealing GPA).
Align with W3C VC Data Model v2.0 and DIDs (did:ethr, did:web).
Mobile holder wallet with secure enclave; NFC/QR offline presentation.
Cross-institution credential federation via multi-tenant IssuerRegistry.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS
21

Designed and built BK Credential System Phase 3 on Ethereum Sepolia,
replacing SD-JWT + IPFS with EIP-712 signing and Merkle tree
anchoring
Key Result:
1.Achieved O(1) on-chain scaling: ~16.8 gas/credential for 10,000-student
batches
2.Offline verification in ~5.5 ms with 100% security test coverage (52 unit
tests, 33 exploit simulations)
3.Learned to balance cryptographic theory with practical engineering
trade-offs in building a real-world system
